abstract.para: &hawk; provides a Batch Mode, including a cluster simulator. Staging changes to the cluster and applying them as a single transaction, instead of having each change take effect immediately. For example, batch mode can be used when creating groups of resources that depend on each other. Using batch mode, you can avoid applying intermediate or incomplete configurations to the cluster.

The cluster simulator runs automatically after every change and shows the expected outcome in the user interface. For example, this also means that if you stop a resource while in batch mode, the user interface shows the resource as stopped, while actually, the resource is still running. Simulating changes and cluster events, for example, to explore potential failure scenarios. It is also possible to simulate events in the cluster, including nodes going online or offline, or resource operations.

important.title: Using wizards in batch mode
important.para: Some wizards include actions beyond cluster configuration, such as installing packages. When using those wizards in batch mode, any changes that go beyond cluster configuration would be applied to the live system immediately.
Therefore, wizards that require &rootuser; permission cannot be used while in batch mode.

step.para: In a Web browser, go to https://HAWKSERVER:7630/ and log in.
In the top-level row, click Batch.
An additional bar appears below the top-level row. It indicates that batch mode is active and contains links to actions that you can perform in batch mode.

While batch mode is active, perform any changes to your cluster, like adding or editing resources and constraints, or editing the cluster configuration. The changes will be simulated and shown in all screens.
To view details of your changes, select Show from the batch mode bar.

The Batch Mode window opens and shows the difference between the live state and the simulated changes in &crmsh; syntax. Lines starting with a - character represent the current state whereas lines starting with + show the proposed state.

listitem.para: Simulate a node failure or status change:
Select the Node you want to manipulate and select its target State.
Confirm your changes. Your event is added to the queue of events listed in the Batch Mode dialog.
Select the Resource you want to manipulate and select the Operation to simulate.
Select the Node on which to run the operation and the targeted Result.
Confirm your changes. Your event is added to the queue of events listed in the Batch Mode dialog.

step.para: The Batch Mode dialog shows a new line per injected event. Any event listed here is simulated immediately and is reflected on the Status screen.
To remove an injected event, click the Remove icon next to it. &hawk; updates the Status screen accordingly.
To view more details about the simulation run, click Simulator and choose one of the following:

listitem.para: CIB (in): Shows the initial CIB state.
CIB (out): Shows what the CIB would look like after the transition.
Transition Graph: Shows a graphical representation of the transition.
Transition: Shows an XML representation of the transition.

step.para: After reviewing your changes, click Close to exit the Batch Mode window.
Choose to either Discard or Apply the simulated changes and confirm your choice. Both options deactivate batch mode and take you back to normal mode.
